body.statement:
For every \(N\in\mathbb N\) and every \(s_N\in(0,1]\) for which \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) is nonempty,
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P L\{\widetilde\mu,\mu(P)\}
\le C_0\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\},
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable estimators based on the entire observed sample.  The covariance-PCA and APM least-squares estimator in \(\operatorname{def:pca-estimator}\) attains this upper bound, with \(C_0\) depending only on the fixed primitive radii and \((T,C)\).
body.justification: The covariance-PCA construction and inverse-modulus bound give the strongest model-wide conclusion valid under the frozen assumptions: an unconditional risk upper bound on every nonempty shell. The legal zero-target subclass rules out a positive universal lower bound.
body.gap: Lei and Ross require the APM gap to dominate estimation noise, while Yan and Wainwright study a different growing-matrix experiment; this theorem supplies a fixed-panel complete-law upper guarantee on the observable singular-margin shell without claiming the refuted universal converse.
body.consumer: Researchers using \(\operatorname{apm}\) or \(\operatorname{fect}\) obtain a sufficient observable signal-to-sample-size condition and a finite-sample risk guarantee for counterfactual recovery.
